name: Digenic Alport Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Alport Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria (adapted for digenic inheritance)

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in two different COL4A genes (e.g., COL4A3 and COL4A4) consistent with digenic inheritance
Persistent microscopic hematuria documented on multiple occasions
Family history of hematuria, renal failure, or hearing loss consistent with Alport syndrome
Electron microscopy showing characteristic glomerular basement membrane abnormalities (thinning, splitting, lamellation)
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, especially in high frequencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic variants in two different COL4A genes plus persistent hematuria and characteristic renal biopsy findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm digenic inheritance; clinical features overlap with other forms of Alport syndrome.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically the earliest and most consistent finding
searchTerms: blood in urine visible only under microscope
tiny amounts of blood in urine

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by electron microscopy on renal biopsy

searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve damage both ears
high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues

common.notes: Characteristic ocular finding in Alport syndrome
May be detected on fundoscopic exam

occasional.notes: Often triggered by exercise or infection
Variable rate of progression to end-stage renal disease

searchTerms: balance problems from inner ear nerve damage

laboratory: Proteinuria detected by urine protein quantification
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen in advanced disease
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or reduced kidney size in advanced disease
Ocular slit-lamp examination revealing anterior lenticonus
Audiometry confirming bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
genetic: Pathogenic variants in two different COL4A genes (e.g., COL4A3 and COL4A4) consistent with digenic inheritance
Absence of variants in COL4A5 gene differentiates from X-linked Alport syndrome
other: Electron microscopy of renal biopsy showing irregular thickening, thinning, and lamellation of glomerular basement membrane

distinguishingFeatures: Inheritance pattern is X-linked with predominant male involvement
Pathogenic variants in COL4A5 gene only
Biallelic pathogenic variants in COL4A3 or COL4A4 genes
Usually early onset with severe renal impairment
Isolated thin glomerular basement membrane without lamellation
Usually benign course with isolated hematuria
No hearing loss or ocular abnormalities

redFlags: Early onset persistent microscopic hematuria with family history
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss in adolescence or early adulthood
Characteristic renal biopsy findings with electron microscopy abnormalities
references: Kashtan CE. Alport syndrome: Achieving clarity on the genetic and clinical spectrum of the disease. Pediatr Nephrol. 2021;36(8):2397-2407.
Savige J, et al. Digenic inheritance of mutations in COL4A3 and COL4A4 genes in Alport syndrome. Kidney Int. 2016;90(5):1004-1010.
